# Glossary

Terms are in alphabetical order. Each chapter links a term here the first time it uses it, and each entry ends with the
chapter where the term is developed.

[AdamW]{#gloss-adamw}
:   The optimizer of the book's training runs: Adam, with weight decay applied to the weights directly and not through
    the gradient. The runs use no weight decay. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[adapter]{#gloss-adapter}
:   The small set of trained matrices that LoRA adds to a frozen model. It is saved on its own, and the base model is
    not changed. See @sec-lora.

[alpha]{#gloss-alpha}
:   The scale of a LoRA update: the correction is multiplied by $\alpha / r$. The sweep sets $\alpha = 2r$, so the
    multiplier is 2 at every rank. See @sec-lora.

[artifact]{#gloss-artifact}
:   A named result saved in `artifacts/`, made by a builder function that a chapter declares. It is rebuilt only when
    it, one of its inputs or the code it uses has changed. See @sec-environment.

[attention]{#gloss-attention}
:   The layer in which each position takes a weighted mix of the values of the positions it can see, with weights from
    the match between its query and their keys. See @sec-anatomy.

[base model]{#gloss-base-model}
:   A model that has only been pretrained to predict the next token of a large body of text, and not post-trained to
    follow instructions. See @sec-base-instruct.

[bfloat16 and mixed precision]{#gloss-bf16}
:   bfloat16 (bf16) is a 16-bit number format with the range of 32-bit floats and fewer digits of precision.
    Mixed-precision training does the arithmetic in bf16 over weights that are kept in 32-bit precision. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[bounded grammar]{#gloss-bounded-grammar}
:   A grammar that also limits each number to the digits that the gold programs use, where the plain grammar allows
    any number. See @sec-constrained-bounds.

[byte-level BPE]{#gloss-bpe}
:   The way Qwen's tokenizer splits text: byte-pair encoding over bytes. It starts from single bytes and merges the
    pairs that occur most often, so any text can be encoded. See @sec-tokens.

[causal mask]{#gloss-causal-mask}
:   The mask that stops a position from attending to the ones after it. It lets one pass over a sequence train the
    prediction at every position, with each prediction seeing only what comes before it. See @sec-anatomy.

[chat template]{#gloss-chat-template}
:   A small program shipped with the tokenizer that wraps each message of a conversation in the model's own role
    markers and joins them into one string. See @sec-base-instruct.

[constrained decoding]{#gloss-constrained-decoding}
:   Decoding in which a grammar removes, at each step, the tokens that cannot continue a valid output. It guarantees
    the form of the output, not that the output ends or is right. See @sec-constrained-decoding.

[cosine schedule]{#gloss-cosine-schedule}
:   The learning rate of the training runs: a short linear warmup to the peak value, then a decay along a cosine curve
    towards zero. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[decoder-only]{#gloss-decoder-only}
:   A transformer made only of decoder blocks, in which every position attends to the earlier ones. Qwen3 is one. See @sec-anatomy.

[development split (dev)]{#gloss-dev}
:   ConvFinQA's own development split, used here as the test set. It is touched only for the final reported numbers,
    after the configuration is frozen. See @sec-formatting.

[DSL]{#gloss-dsl}
:   The domain-specific language of ConvFinQA's programs: a list of steps such as `divide(#0, 181001)`, each with one
    of six operations, where `#k` is the result of an earlier step. See @sec-dsl.

[effective batch]{#gloss-effective-batch}
:   The number of conversations whose gradients are combined for one optimizer step. When they do not fit in memory at
    once, gradient accumulation reaches it with several smaller micro-batches. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[effective number of directions]{#gloss-effective-directions}
:   For a LoRA update, $1 / \sum p^2$, where $p$ is the share of its squared norm held by each direction. It equals
    the rank if the directions share the norm evenly, and 1 if one direction holds all of it. See @sec-rank-loss.

[entropy]{#gloss-entropy}
:   A measure of how spread out a probability distribution over the next token is: zero when one token has all the
    probability, and largest when every token is equally likely. See @sec-tokens.

[example set]{#gloss-example-set}
:   A fixed group of complete training conversations written into a prompt as examples. See @sec-baseline.

[execution accuracy]{#gloss-execution-accuracy}
:   The share of turns where the answer of the model's program equals the gold answer after rounding to five decimal
    places. An output that is not a valid program, or does not execute, counts as wrong. See @sec-dsl and @sec-evaluating.

[exposure bias]{#gloss-exposure-bias}
:   The mismatch left by teacher forcing: the model is trained on gold earlier turns, but when it is used it sees its
    own earlier outputs, which can be wrong. See @sec-base-instruct.

[few-shot and zero-shot]{#gloss-few-shot}
:   A prompt is few-shot when it contains worked examples, and zero-shot when it has none. See @sec-probing.

[full fine-tuning]{#gloss-full-fine-tuning}
:   Training every weight of the model, where LoRA trains a small adapter. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[gold history and predicted history]{#gloss-gold-history}
:   The two ways to fill the earlier turns of a prompt when a conversation is scored. With gold history they are the
    dataset's own programs; with predicted history they are the model's own outputs, mistakes included, so errors can
    compound. Predicted history is the headline setting. See @sec-baseline.

[gradient accumulation and clipping]{#gloss-gradient-accumulation}
:   Accumulation adds up the gradients of several micro-batches before one optimizer step. Clipping rescales a gradient
    whose norm is above a limit. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[grammar]{#gloss-grammar}
:   A formal description of the outputs that are allowed. Here it is a context-free grammar written in EBNF, for the
    DSL or for Python. See @sec-constrained-decoding.

[greedy decoding]{#gloss-greedy}
:   Choosing the highest-scoring token at every step. It is deterministic, and every evaluation of the book uses it
    unless it says otherwise. See @sec-tokens.

[grouped-query attention]{#gloss-gqa}
:   Attention in which several query heads share one key and value head, which makes the KV cache smaller. See @sec-anatomy.

[instruct model]{#gloss-instruct-model}
:   A base model that has been post-trained to follow instructions and to answer in a chat format. See @sec-base-instruct.

[invalid output]{#gloss-invalid-output}
:   An output that is not a valid program or does not execute. It counts as wrong, and the evaluation reports its share
    next to the accuracy, by cause. See @sec-evaluating.

[KV cache]{#gloss-kv-cache}
:   The keys and values of every token already processed, kept so that generating the next token does not recompute
    them. See @sec-anatomy.

[labels]{#gloss-labels}
:   The tokens that the loss is computed on. In this book they are the answer tokens and their end marker; every other
    token of a conversation is masked out. See @sec-formatting.

[learning rate]{#gloss-learning-rate}
:   The size of the step that the optimizer takes along the gradient. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[literal check]{#gloss-literal-check}
:   A check on the numbers a program is written with: whether they match those of the gold program, as text and as
    values, and whether each comes from the page. See @sec-evaluating.

[logits]{#gloss-logits}
:   The scores that the model gives to every token of its vocabulary at a position, before they are turned into
    probabilities. See @sec-tokens.

[logits processor]{#gloss-logits-processor}
:   A function that edits the logits after the model produces them and before a token is chosen. Constrained decoding
    is one. See @sec-tokens.

[LoRA]{#gloss-lora}
:   Low-rank adaptation: the weights of the model are frozen, and each adapted matrix gets an update that is the
    product of two thin matrices, so only those are trained. See @sec-lora.

[loss]{#gloss-loss}
:   The number that training makes smaller: the negative log probability that the model gives to the gold tokens,
    averaged over the label tokens. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[main run]{#gloss-main-run}
:   The LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3-4B on the DSL whose adapter the later chapters use. See @sec-training.

[merging an adapter]{#gloss-merging}
:   Adding the adapter's update into the base weights, so the model runs without the adapter. It is the same function
    in 32-bit precision and not exactly in bf16. See @sec-lora.

[negative log-likelihood]{#gloss-nll}
:   The loss of a sequence: the sum, or mean, of the surprisals of its tokens. See @sec-probing.

[number-selection turn]{#gloss-number-selection}
:   A turn whose program is only a number copied from the page, with no operation. All other turns are lists of steps.
    See @sec-dsl.

[paired bootstrap]{#gloss-paired-bootstrap}
:   An interval for the difference between two systems scored on the same turns. It resamples whole conversations,
    since the turns of one conversation are not independent, and computes both accuracies on each resample. An interval
    that excludes zero is a clear difference. See @sec-baseline-rule.

[perplexity]{#gloss-perplexity}
:   The exponential of the mean surprisal: the model is as uncertain, on average, as if it were choosing among that
    many equally likely tokens. See @sec-probing.

[post-training]{#gloss-post-training}
:   The training that turns a pretrained model into an instruct model, such as supervised fine-tuning, distillation and
    reinforcement learning. See @sec-base-instruct.

[pretraining]{#gloss-pretraining}
:   The first stage of training, in which the model learns to predict the next token on a large body of text. See @sec-base-instruct.

[program accuracy]{#gloss-program-accuracy}
:   The share of turns where the model's program is the gold program by the rule of the official ConvFinQA script: the
    programs are compared as expressions, so the operands of `add` and `multiply` may come in either order, and the
    arguments are compared as exact text. It is stricter than execution accuracy. See @sec-evaluating.

[QLoRA]{#gloss-qlora}
:   LoRA on a base model whose weights are stored in a low-precision, quantized format, to save memory. See @sec-lora.

[rank]{#gloss-rank}
:   The number of directions between the two thin matrices of a LoRA update, and so the largest rank the update can
    have. See @sec-lora.

[rank sweep]{#gloss-rank-sweep}
:   The same fine-tuning run at several values of the LoRA rank, compared on the same turns. See @sec-rank-sweep.

[residual connection]{#gloss-residual}
:   The addition of a layer's input to its output, so the layer learns a change to its input and not a replacement.
    See @sec-anatomy.

[rotary position embedding]{#gloss-rope}
:   The way Qwen3 encodes position: queries and keys are rotated by an angle that depends on the position, so an
    attention score depends on the distance between two tokens. See @sec-anatomy.

[sampling and temperature]{#gloss-sampling}
:   Sampling draws the next token from the probabilities. The temperature divides the logits first: a low value
    sharpens the distribution towards greedy decoding, and a high one flattens it. See @sec-tokens.

[scale check]{#gloss-scale-check}
:   A check on whether an answer is the gold answer times, or divided by, a power of ten, which is a different mistake
    from a wrong number. See @sec-evaluating.

[self-consistency]{#gloss-self-consistency}
:   Sampling several programs at a temperature, dropping those that do not run, and taking the answer that most of them
    agree on. See @sec-evaluating.

[singular values]{#gloss-singular-values}
:   The strengths of the independent directions of a matrix. For a LoRA update they show how its size is spread over
    its directions. See @sec-training.

[smoke run]{#gloss-smoke-run}
:   A short run of the 0.5B model with the same recipe, to test the training code before the main run. See @sec-training.

[softmax]{#gloss-softmax}
:   The function that turns logits into probabilities that are positive and sum to one. See @sec-tokens.

[supervised fine-tuning (SFT)]{#gloss-sft}
:   Training a model on example outputs with a next-token loss. See @sec-base-instruct.

[surprisal]{#gloss-surprisal}
:   The negative log of the probability the model gave to a token, in nats. See @sec-probing.

[system message]{#gloss-system-message}
:   The first message of a prompt, which tells the model what its task and its output format are. See @sec-baseline.

[teacher forcing]{#gloss-teacher-forcing}
:   Training with the gold earlier tokens or turns in the input, whatever the model would have produced. See @sec-base-instruct.

[token and tokenizer]{#gloss-token}
:   A token is a piece of text, usually a word or part of one, that the model reads and writes as one unit. The
    tokenizer turns text into token ids and back. See @sec-tokens.

[train-fit]{#gloss-train-fit}
:   The part of the training data that a run trains on: the training split without the validation conversations. See @sec-training.

[Type I and Type II conversations]{#gloss-conversation-types}
:   Type I conversations break one FinQA question into a chain of turns. Type II conversations join two questions about
    the same page. See @sec-convfinqa.

[validation split]{#gloss-validation}
:   A tenth of the training conversations, grouped by page, held out for the choices of the book. The tuning is done
    on it, and the development split is kept for the final numbers. See @sec-formatting.

[warmup]{#gloss-warmup}
:   The first steps of a run, in which the learning rate rises linearly from zero to its peak. See @sec-fine-tuning.

[weight decay]{#gloss-weight-decay}
:   A term that pulls each weight a little towards zero at every step. See @sec-fine-tuning.
